pr_title: ipc: Enable no-copy features in icmsg backend
pr_body:
The icmsg_me (me stands for multi-endpoint) backend has no-copy features that in fact are implemented in icmsg.c. The icmsg backend should be configurable to have these no-copy features, too.

This fixes #62558 .
pr_comments:
> I remember discussing with @emob-nordic that icmsg is well-designed for control messages, but it does not work well for the data plane and should be supplemented with a data buffer allocation mechanism like a heap, slabs, pool, network buffers, etc. The no-copy feature is useful almost exclusively for the data plane and because of this, it was considered to remove this feature from the icmsg library.
> 
> I don't remember the conclusion of this discussion.

The plan is to remove no copy rx/tx feature from icmsg library. My intention here is to make icmsg as simplest as possible and to be used in restricted use cases (mostly with high memory constraints).

Icmsg is meant to be used to send relatively small data packets where no-copy feature does not give significant benefits thus will be removed to reduce code complexity.

That does not mean we will no longer support no-copy feature in icmsg based backend. We plan to implement this in new backend https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/pull/58741 that will distinguish control and data plane. Control plane is for sending control messages (sending, receiving, claiming buffers, etc.) - icmsg will be base for it, data plane is exclusively for plain data - no-copy will be supported there.

Note that initial plan assumes icmsg_me removal.

Please let me know what your use case is and if we could adapt the development plan to it so we could satisfy both.

Hi Sorry for the delay. My use case is I have an NXP board with a Cortex-M33 core and a DSP, and I want to use icmsg to send audio data back and forth. The audio data is 1KiB~4KiB in size so I would really like to do that without copying. The M33 core and the DSP already have shared memory. I just want to have icmsg manage the buffer allocation and freeing for me. Without icmsg I would have to manually manage my buffers allocated from shared memory.

Thanks.

I just want to have icmsg manage the buffer allocation and freeing for me. Without icmsg I would have to manually manage my buffers allocated from shared memory.

icmsg is not designed to send big data chunks. In the near future no-copy will be removed. For your case i would suggest you to either:
- check out #58741 where allocation and buffer management will be done for you (no-copy supported)
- implement your own allocator with no-copy support and send pointer to allocated memory with icmsg. You could even use existing heap/memslab/net_buf or other allocators if they fit your solution.

My recomendation for you would be to try out #58741 and submit your concerns there. I'm currently reviewing it and will push to finalize that part asap.

Please let me know in case of any doubts or questions.

issue_context.title: ipc: icmsg: Support no-copy sending and receiving in icmsg backend
issue_context.body:
**Is your enhancement proposal related to a problem? Please describe.**
Currently only the `icmsg_me` (multi-endpoint) backend supports the [no-copy API](https://docs.zephyrproject.org/latest/services/ipc/ipc_service/ipc_service.html#data-exchange-using-the-no-copy-api). When using the [icmsg backend](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/main/subsys/ipc/ipc_service/backends/ipc_icmsg.c) for two endpoints, one would expect no-copy API to be available, but it's not.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Implement the following API in the [icmsg backend](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/main/subsys/ipc/ipc_service/backends/ipc_icmsg.c):
- get_tx_buffer()
- drop_tx_buffer()
- send_nocopy()
- hold_rx_buffer()
- release_rx_buffer()

The implementation will just call the corresponding APIs in [the icmsg lib](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/main/subsys/ipc/ipc_service/lib/icmsg.c). This implementation is really cheap and simple. The `icmsg_me` backend already does this. We can just do the same thing in the `icmsg` backend.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Alternative would be trying to use `icmsg_me` for two-endpoint case for no-copy sending/receiving. This feels unnatural.

**Additional context**
N/A

review_comments: I think it would be cleaner if instead of relying on a icmsg library configuration (`IPC_SERVICE_ICMSG_NOCOPY_RX`) you create a new `IPC_SERVICE_BACKEND_ICMSG_NOCOPY_RX` in a new file like ipc_service/backends/Kconfig.icmsg to configure the icmsg backend.
